blocks.text: Coquitlam West, in the City of Coquitlam, is a real estate board name for the west side of the city, toward the Burnaby border, around Burquitlam, Austin Heights, and Como Lake Avenue. Burquitlam Station on the Millennium Line is the local SkyTrain stop. North Road is the municipal boundary street with Burnaby’s Lougheed Town Centre.

Homes for sale in Coquitlam West include apartments and townhouses closer to the station and North Road, and houses on the Austin Heights and Como Lake side streets. Mundy Park sits to the east. Shops gather on Austin, Clarke, and North Road.

The Millennium Line at Burquitlam and buses on Austin, Como Lake, and North Road connect to Lougheed Town Centre and Coquitlam Central Station. Nearby public schools include those in the Burquitlam and Austin Heights families. Check the SD43 school locator.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Coquitlam West

items.t: Established-street house lots: single-detached streets under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, while apartment buildings cluster near the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations under the Transit-Oriented Areas framework.

Lot sizes (Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996): new lots must be at least 650 m² and 18.5 m wide in R-1 and R-3, or 465 m² and 12.5 m wide in R-2. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam's SSMUH framework expressly leaves lots not connected to municipal water or sewer outside the SSMUH rules, which is the City's own servicing qualifier for house lots here; Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste.
Check a specific parcel through the Agricultural Land Commission before applying any ALR rule.

Flooding and creeks: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers everything within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam, and the Zoning Bylaw adds flood and streamside setbacks.

Market figures, September 2026 (homes, not land): in Coquitlam West, 76 detached homes were listed and 2 sold (3%), and 359 condos and townhomes were listed and 35 sold (10%). Coquitlam's medians were $1,455,000 for detached homes and $625,000 for condos and townhomes.
Burquitlam Park District (Intergulf, Clarke Road and Como Lake Avenue) is a presale development. It sells strata homes, not lots.
A 29-storey tower plus a 6-storey wood-frame building, with 246 condos and four townhouses.

Southwest Shoulders and Corridors (adopted): the City's Transit-Oriented Areas Update and the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors review produced OCP and Zoning amendments creating medium-density housing and townhousing opportunities around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations and along Austin Avenue; the City states Council adopted the amendments following a public hearing. Whether a specific lot sits inside an amended area is a City confirmation for that parcel — the amendment map, not a listing claim, decides assembly value.

items.t: Coquitlam West is the City of Coquitlam's south-west side. The City plans the same area as Southwest Coquitlam, covering the neighbourhoods around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre SkyTrain stations and along Austin Avenue.
Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the east, Maillardville to the south-east, Port Moody to the north-west, and Burnaby (Lougheed / Cariboo) across North Road to the west.

Main roads: North Road, Clarke Road, Austin Avenue and Lougheed Highway. Transit: Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines).

Civic anchors in this part of the city: Coquitlam Public Library Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street (City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, serves Coquitlam as a whole); Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border.
Schools: School District 43 catchments are address-based and SD43 is a three-tier district. School names are.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Coquitlam West

items.t: Plan: the Interim Official Community Plan, Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026, supersedes OCP No. 3479. The adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments sit inside that framework for the station areas and Austin Avenue.

Creeks: a watercourse development permit can be needed within 30 metres of the top of any creek bank, along with flood and streamside setbacks, so check slope and creek lots before pricing a lot split or extra unit.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Coquitlam property taxes and utilities: City of Coquitlam property tax payment was due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants); utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste, and the City's 2026 budget materials record an average-household total property-charges increase of $137.

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026 (dated fact): the Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511/5512) was adopted April 27, 2026, superseding OCP No. 3479. Any page, listing package or assembly pitch still citing OCP No. 3479 as the current plan is out of date.

New townhouses here will come from a plan, not existing buildings: the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments were adopted to allow townhouses around the two SkyTrain stations and Austin Avenue. For any "land value" pitch, first check whether the lot is inside that area.

items.t: Municipality: City of Coquitlam, BC — Coquitlam West is the city's south-west side; the City's planning area for the same area is Southwest Coquitlam, which includes the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor.

Main roads and transit: North Road, Clarke Road, Austin Avenue and Lougheed Highway serve Coquitlam West. Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines) serve the sub-area.

Both manufactured-home parks are in Maillardville on the south side: Wildwood Park on Cayer Street and Mill Creek Village on King Edward Street, on flat, walkable streets south of the station areas where the towers are.
Schools: School District 43 catchments are address-based (three-tier).

items.t: Wildwood Park is not a 55+ park, though it turns up in Tri-Cities park searches. It is large, established (over 30 years per its operator's description), amenity-rich and affordable-looking, and it is family-oriented, with a playground in its own listing copy. Wildwood Park at 201 Cayer St does not belong on a 55+ shortlist; searches sometimes group it with the genuinely 55+ Hideaway Park across the city.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: No known one — the area is established station-area strata plus interior house streets.

faq.q: How many homes can a house lot here carry under SSMUH?
faq.a: Up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes — and only where the lot is connected to municipal water and sewer; unserviced lots fall outside the rules.

faq.q: Does a lot near Burquitlam or Lougheed station carry redevelopment value?
faq.a: Possibly — the adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments create medium-density and townhousing opportunities around both stations and along Austin Avenue. Whether the specific lot is inside an amended area is a City confirmation, not a listing claim.

faq.q: Is a Coquitlam West house lot serviced?
faq.a: The City's framework assumes municipal water and sewer for SSMUH eligibility and bills water, sewer/drainage and solid waste as City utilities.

faq.q: What servicing bylaw governs a subdivision here?
faq.a: The Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — works and services must be provided to the City's standards under that bylaw, confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.

faq.q: What mobile-home buying actually exists in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: Two pad-rental parks in the Maillardville pocket: Wildwood Park (201 Cayer St) and Mill Creek Village (145 King Edward St). In both, you own the home and rent the pad. There is no 55+ park, no bare-land strata park and no co-op park verified in this sub-area.

faq.q: In either park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Plainly, a home on a rented pad is not land ownership. Wildwood's listings say it directly: leasehold, non-strata, on rented pads.

faq.q: Is Wildwood Park a 55+ park? It keeps coming up in 55+ searches.
faq.a: No. Wildwood Park at 201 Cayer St is marketed in its own listings as a family-oriented park with a playground, pool, tennis court and clubhouse, on leasehold non-strata pads. Its appearance in 55+ searches is a search artefact from grouping with Hideaway Park across the city.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve Coquitlam West?
faq.a: Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines); the City's Southwest Coquitlam planning is built around those two station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor.

faq.q: What planning change affects Coquitlam West houses?
faq.a: The adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors OCP and Zoning amendments, creating medium-density housing and townhousing opportunities around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations and along Austin Avenue, on top of the citywide SSMUH rules (up to 3–4 units on house lots).
